newsitem.title: USA: State judge throws out county law banning jet skis.
newsitem.headline: State judge throws out county law banning jet skis.

text.p: A Washington state judge on Monday overturned a law banning motorized "water-bikes" from the picturesque San Juan islands in a victory for manufacturers of the popular but noisy craft.

Whatcom County Superior Court Judge Steven ruled that San Juan County's 8-month-old outright ban on motorized personal watercraft was too broad and granted the industry's request for an injunction preventing enforcement.
Mura said that when the state licenses the boats it implies they may be used on state waters including those around the archipelago 70 miles (125 km) north of Seattle.
"If every county were to outlaw these the state would allow people to own them but not to use them," Mura said.
The case, brought by an industry trade group and several county businesses, was seen as a test of efforts nationwide to restrict the boats commonly known by the trade name Jet Skis.
San Juan County's law was perhaps the nation's most extreme anti-Jet Ski measure, adopted after 1,500 of the tourism-dependent county's 12,000 residents petitioned to ban the watercraft.

The manufacturers group, which includes Kawasaki Heavy Industries Inc., Yamaha Corp. and Polaris Industries Inc., sued on the grounds that the waters around the 172 islands were considered public highways and thus open to all boaters.
Roger Hagie of the Personal Watercraft Industry Association said the ruling affirms that water-bikers "are boaters and should enjoy the same rights as other boaters."
San Juan County Prosecutor Randall Gaylord said county officials had not decided whether to appeal.
Jeffrey Johnson, lead attorney for the industry group, said manufacturers would fight any appeal. "The industry remains willing to work with the county to develop restrictions," he said.
